notes.title: What’s Next for Our Adventurer Guild?
notes.content:
Hello Guild Masters,

It has been a while since my last announcement, so I thought it was time to share my plans moving forward. I have both good news and bad news.

The Bad News
Let’s start with the bad news. In my last announcement, I mentioned that I was evaluating whether adding modding support for the game would be feasible. Unfortunately, after spending a considerable amount of time trying to build a foundation for modding, I fear that it won’t happen.

I underestimated the amount of work required, and while I could try to work around some of the flaws in my initial designs, it would take a significant amount of time and I want to be honest here: 

I want to move on from OAG. 

OAG was my first game, and while I’m incredibly grateful and happy that so many of you enjoy it, I still see it as rough around the edges. Instead of forcing modding into this version, I’d rather make it a reality in a potential sequel—one that’s more polished from the start.

I’m sorry to disappoint those who were hoping for modding support. However, while I won’t be releasing dedicated modding tools, I will be adding more options to modify certain aspects of the game. Specifically, I plan to add the ability to add custom translations and the ability to replace some of the music if you’d like.

The Good News
Now for the good news! I don’t want to end my support for the game on that note, so I’ve decided to create a DLC. Alongside it, I’ll be releasing a final free content update that incorporates some of your feedback. With these additions, I believe OAG will be in a good state, allowing me to move forward with my next game.

I’ve already started working on the DLC and will share more details in future announcements. For now, here’s a splash art to give you a little teaser:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42498874/a09f9b4f789ae787183fdfa9cfff4f249fbb4c0f.png

Additional Language Support
I’d also like to announce that the next two languages to receive support have been decided! Translation work has begun for Korean and Chinese, and they will most likely be ready in about 3-4 months.

With best regards
GreenGuy

notes.title: Patch 1.3 is live and Future Plans
notes.content:
Hello Guild Masters,

Patch 1.3 is live and includes some bug fixes that have been reported so far. There shouldn't be anything game-breaking now and NG+ is good to go.

Now, I'd like to talk about what I plan to do next now that NG+ is done.

Controller Support
A lot of people have requested controller support, and I think that would be a good thing. This is most likely the next item on my to-do list. However, I need to be honest here:

I don't know if it will happen.

Much of the UI won't work with controller input out of the box and will need specific handling or even a redesign. To complicate matters, it has been ages since I played a game with controllers, so I'm not very familiar with current design philosophies.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42498874/534146f780025de9db14fbd103c2b1f5a7dc28c5.png
Honestly, no idea how this is supposed to work with a controller.

Still, I want to attempt it and will dedicate at least a month to it. But if it seems like the undertaking would be too much, I might just put it further down the line or drop it entirely.

Mod Support/Custom Content
This is something I want to add after I complete or attempt the controller support. It's something I'd love to have in my game, and it would be great to see what the community could create. There are certain things I want to be possible to add:


 Create custom Quests
 Create custom Events
 Create custom Items
 Create custom Hairstyles
 Create custom Faces
 Create custom Classes
 Create custom Skills
 Create custom Titles


This would also be completely new to me, and because the game was originally not designed for it, it could be a huge undertaking.

DLCs
This would be the very last thing on the list. If all the previous points are behind me, I need to see if and what kind of DLC I want to do. But I do not believe that I would do more than one DLC. It has been more than 3 years since I started working on OAG, and it seems likely I will stick to it for another year. However, after that, I would like to close this chapter in my life and start a new project. I know this might sound disappointing, but I hope that if I accomplish mod support, players will be able to create enough custom content for the game to stay alive for a long time, even without me.

That's everything I wanted to say, and I hope you continue to have fun with the game.

With best regards,
GreenGuy

notes.title: Patch 1.3 Beta NG+
notes.content:
Hello Guild Masters,

The NG+ update is finally here with Patch 1.3! This patch introduces a host of changes and improvements. In addition to adding NG+, there are many other updates and bug fixes. Due to the number of changes and the fact that a save in Patch 1.3 cannot be safely loaded in a previous game version, Patch 1.3 will be released as a Beta Patch for now. I will continue testing this patch until Thursday, and if everything seems fine, I will set it live on the main branch. On Thursday, I will also announce my plans going forward.

NG+

How does NG+ work? After completing the final story quest, you can start NG+ with that save file. To start NG+, go to your saves in the main menu and select a save file that qualifies for NG+. Valid saves are marked accordingly.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42498874/40b7876e0f82d5a4de01f081ef5e4a004f64ab08.png

Here, you can decide what to take with you. You can bring any adventurers and items. You can also apply modifiers to your NG+ run that can significantly change your new adventure. - Added NG+:
- Reworked the skills for the Warlord title. "Act Now" costs 3 AP and will now end the title holder's turn and give the target an immediate additional turn on which they can act. The target will get strained for one turn, which will reduce their damage by 30% and prevents them from using Brave Actions. "Stay in Reserved" is now called "Retreat" and will have the same effect as "Act Now" but also get a 3 Movement Buff, +50 Dodge, +50 Block and a -3AP debuff. It also cost 3AP now. - Added several new legendary items
- Removed Unity splash screen
- Updated the Splash art for the Knight Class

  QuestmapEnemyStandardMapSpeed=0.7 
SmallQuestMapEventMinAmount=1

notes.title: The Emperor Update is here!
notes.content:
Hello Guild Masters,

the Emperor Update is finally here!
It took longer than I wanted but it's finally done and I'd like to share with you whats in it.

What's in store for you:


 Concluding the main story with two main quests
 New quest location
 Two new legendary classes with their own unique skill tree
 Fresh traits to explore
 new events
 5 new side quests
 more enemies and bosses
 legendary weapons and armor


Also Bugfixes and Changes:
I've also worked on a lot of bugfixes and changes, from the feedback I've gathered over the last few days. More details in the patch notes.

What's Next:
While this marks the last major content update before the full release, the journey doesn't end here. There are still loose ends and unfinished aspects that need attention.(The new Quest location for example has only 3 events, or Ferdinands questline still doesn't have an ending.)

Current my priority looks like this:
Bugfixes for bugs that might occur due to this patch: There should be nothing game breaking here but you'll never know. So I keep an eye out for any such reports and fix them as soon as possible.

UI/Quality of Life: There are a lot of rough edges here, and some aspect of the game are tedious because of supbar UI. I will be working on improving this. Interacting with the UI should feel good. Not tedious.

Balancing: Some classes may need fine-tuning to ensure they're not left behind by others. There might also be inconsistency with the game challenge in the middle to later part.

Completing Loose Ends: I'll be tying up loose ends like Ferdinands Questline and adding ways to remove Misasas bad trait. There also a few enemies in the game, that haven't been fully integrated yet.

Minor Content Additions: Adding more titles, dialogues, items, side stories, events, and other things to round up the whole package.

Steam Achievements!

Polishing: Your feedback is important here. If anything feels rough or could be improved, don't hesitate to report it. Even the smallest details

I also plan to add controller support, but depending on how it goes I might add it after the full release.

Well, that's all. I hope you'll have fun with the new content and hopefully your feedback can help create a great 1.0 version of the game!

I'll be putting the game on a small sale to celebrate the new update. Afterwards the price will be raise to its final value of about 15$.

With Best Regards
GreenGuy

notes.title: Witch Update - Overview
notes.content:
Hello Guild Masters,

this might be a little late since the content update has been life more than a day now but still I wanted to do use this announcement as an opportunity to go into detail what has changed and there has been a lot of changes.

New Content:

4 new Main Quest, 3 Sidequests
3 new classes:

Dragon Knight
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42498874/45f60d5a1afa7ef2d78f9e7fa32491d98f7a99fd.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42498874/718110c2fc0e8758185d4be6085bdf2501e6363d.png
Witch
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42498874/fdeec16bff70d903ec21e1b7d7b13d5bd752d866.png


over a dozen new enemies
new traits
new skills
new items:

the first legendary items
monk armor
3 demonic weapons
new enhancement gems



New mechanics:

1. Elevation:
The biggest change in combat is the inclusion of elevation. There are several maps now that can be pulled in random battles where the map is not completely flat and the new quests with their own battle maps have been designed to include the new changes. I will revisit the older quests to make elevation a part of them too. Also the amount of different maps for the generic quests are still limited but i plan to add more with time. 

So what does elevation do? Well, first and foremost it affects how units can interact with each other. Skills now have a "Height Tolerance value". 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42498874/ebe9b2a7ace6e7030ba905052dabbddedbbfd1dd.png
The height tolerance value indicates how height affects the skill. The left value tells you how big the height difference between the target and you can be at most, for the target to be selectable by the skill
The right value plays a role for skills that affect multiple tiles. In this case the value tells you how big the height difference between the surrounding tiles and the selected tile can be at most for them to be also affected by the skill.

Another thing that elevation affects is hitchances. Character at higher elevation gain a bonus to hitchance of 10 for every tile higher than their opponent.

I will update the tutorial in the future to include this new mechanic

2. Holy vs. Darkness
With the inclusion of the witch update two new damage types have been introduced. Holy damage and Dark damage. Skills have been adjusted to account for these changes, and demons and undead now have lower resistance to holy damage.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42498874/885aab6e2fa09e171f477611e9e967cfea2fba77.png

3. Stances
Skills that can be toggled on and off for buffs have been introduced. Many of these skills will either drain SP over time or impose debuffs on other aspects. A few skills will be updated to utilize this new mechanic instead of providing flat bonuses.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42498874/3424b37c725a8a34855b4c7bec36dffa4961d162.png
4. Martial Arts Skill tree
The Monk Skill tree has been divided to create a new skill tree called "Martial Arts," available to both the monk and sword master classes.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42498874/e6923762b548220c4a928b628e38eaf3cc14e468.png


Now what's next?
First I will concentrate on fixing any bug that will pop up for this update and I expect a whole lot more. Then I will take some time to create a demo for the game. Afterwards I will also work on adding some minor contents I had in mind for this update but didn't make it. And then finally, I will start working on the final update: the Emperor Update.

Well that's all for this announcement.
I wish you all a good day :)

With best regards
TheGreenGuy

notes.title: The Saintess Patch (0.6250) is Live!
notes.content:
Hey Guild Masters,

This took a little longer than I anticipated, but it's finally completed now. :) There is a lot of new content in this patch, and I hope it adds some more hours of gameplay for you.

1 new quest location with 10 new events.
18 new enemies.
6 new story quests (1 Main Quest, 3 NPC-Quests, 2 Powerful Monster Quests).

A new set of repeatable assignments that allow you to hunt previously encountered major monsters to acquire their materials.
6 new Guild Events.
9 new camping dialogues related to an adventurer's death during a quest.

I've tried my best to ensure that the update is compatible with existing savegame and I had no trouble with the old save I've been testing. Nevertheless, starting a new game is the safest way to guarantee the visibility of all the new content.

In the upcoming days, I plan to work on the missing sidestories that I initially promised for this update. Additionally, I'll be adding more customization options (new hairstyles and faces) to the game. There's also a new unique character I intend to introduce as a recruitable member. While you'll encounter her in this update, the event to recruit her hasn't been implemented yet.

I'll be releasing a proper roadmap tomorrow, or at the latest, the day after, to provide you with a clear idea of the current plan.

Best regards,
TheGreenGuy

notes.title: Patch 0.5122
notes.content:
So, I wanted to announce a small gameplay update that will go live tomorrow(If everything goes well) and like to introduce a new patch numbering system that will continue until the 1.0 launch.

From now on patches will get a version number and it follows the following pattern(Let's declare the current state as Version 0.5022):

 Major Content Update: Changing the first digit after the point (e.g., 0.5022 -> 0.6022)
 Small Updates: Changing the second digit after the point (e.g., 0.5022 -> 0.5122)
 Bug Fixes: Changing the 3rd and 4th digits after the point (e.g., 0.5022 -> 0.5023)


Following this pattern the next patch will be 0.5122 which will include a new battle mechanic, some small updates to the monk class and Hotkeys.

Gameplay Changes:
Currently there are several skills that can shove enemies in a direction. It didn't do much besides just moving an enemy away. By itself those skills weren't really interesting so I thought I'd add some depths into it by adding collision damage.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42498874/c286914f1f3fef887db6406375d831827d728d3e.gif


 When an enemy is pushed into an obstacle, they will receive collision damage.
 Pushing an enemy into another enemy inflicts damage on both, while pushing an enemy into an ally increases collision damage.
 The amount of collision damage scales with the distance traveled and the level of the target, ensuring its relevance at higher levels. (Note: The damage formula may be adjusted based on feedback.)
 This change also allows for future obstacles on battle maps that utilize this mechanic.


Monk Update:
Monks were still quite lacking in their skill diversity. I wanted to address it with this patch by adding some interesting skill options for them:
- {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42498874/981152df0148a5a428c76b90444dc51c39e4a34d.pngOpening Strike. A simple skill where the monk will charge through an enemy push them back. Especially good if you've got another enemy behind you
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42498874/acaf16f8b4635643ff727284d852c2185386e0aa.gif
- {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42498874/900c7f85365095c90c4d7d5d844f5476aaa4d927.pngKi Shockwave. Just like Ki strike, this skill deals true damage but in AOE.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42498874/2ac331a3f577f43db46ae746a95e54fa3dd4a968.gif
- {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42498874/7e83ccc1c40ab36d599057f0ed86cce79f261372.pngAnaconda Strike. A strike that continues to travel through every enemy behind the first target and pushes the final target
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42498874/e7ca074f351d6af9a90fa2abdfea8a49b79c8538.gif

The monk skill tree will be updated to include these new skills. Two new skills will provide access to multiple skills, aligning with the design of other classes:

At level 8, there will be now the skill "Basic Monk Techniques" that holds the following skills:

 Ki Strike
 Opening Strike


At level 16, there will be now the skill "Advanced Monk Techniques" that holds the following skills:

 Ki Shockwave
 Anaconda Strike


Lastly, there will be additional hotkeys available for exploration and combat as quality-of-life changes. The options menu will allow you to customize keybindings.

- Level Requirement for skill "Stalwart Protection" has been corrected to level 20. Any adventurer who had that skill will lose the skill on returning to the guild if they don't satisfy the requirements. You will be refunded the skillpoint.

notes.title: Minor Fixes 08
notes.content:
- Fixed an issue where monks without a weapon are considered insufficiently equipped. Now the warning shouldn't appear anymore
- Fixed in issue where adventurers could be trained if they were below the level threshold but had already enough exp to level up. Now adventurers who have reached the experience threshold for the current level have to level up first before they can be trained
- Fixed an issue where when a character dies while passing a trap tile, the trap tile would be considered occupied for the rest of the battle
- After much confusion about the talking sword questline, a subobjective has been added to clarify that the questline is unfinished but not over yet
- Fixed an issue where after upgrading Ferdinand, he would become a different weapon type. If an adventurer has equipped Ferdinand with wrong weapon type, it will be unequipped now when returning/loading into the Guild

notes.title: Minor Fixes 07
notes.content:
- Fixed an issue where completing a quest and encountering an enemy at the same time could cause the quest not being resolved properly
- Fixed an issue with the quest "Routed Army". The decision for an ambush with an bow was available despite no adventurers having a bow. This could cause a problem when a check was required next. Now the decision is only available when there is an archer in the party

notes.title: Minor Fixes 06
notes.content:
- Fixed an issue that could cause a dialogue scene to break
- Added some QOL changes
- Nerfed the Trait "Talented"

notes.title: So what's next
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

it has been a week now since I launched the game in early access and it has been a rocky start ^^;.
Thanks to everyone who has been reporting bugs and I hope the worst of the bugs are gone now. I hope you had at least a bit of fun with the game, despite the bugs.

So, what's next? What else is there on the horizon?

Well, right now besides playing exterminator on any bug encountered, I'm also currently working on the next content. Currently, I have planned to include the following content in the next content update:

- A new Quest location with new challenges and monsters:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42498874/b8e212d7185dc7d58b5e6331380ea7334c881482.png 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42498874/88d7d7acbad1e2d78dc4fb76f3fd6ff45373f7b0.gif

- More optional boss monsters to hunt:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42498874/349eefbd7d2bc0e577f9fe309c782e4737720c66.gif

- More items at higher rarities
- A fully functional title system. The current one is a WIP and is very rough around the edges. It needs tweaking and overhauling.
- The next step in the Main Quest and some more side quests
- The first legendary class. Legendary classes differ from ordinary class in that only one adventurer at a time can learn it. In exchange for that limitation, they'll become the most powerful adventurers in your roster.
- Elevation(This is still something I have to consider if I want it in the next content update or the one after).

I hope to be able to deliver the content update in 1-2 months. Of course I will also keep an eye on any bugs that get reported. 

Thanks for playing the game and I wish you the best!
TheGreenGuy
